text.label: Part one — How she talks
text.value: Part one — How she talks

text.label: Before anything else, she has to not sound like software.
text.value: Before anything else, she has to not sound like software.

text.label: 1 · Like a friend, not a brochure
text.value: 1 · Like a friend, not a brochure

text.label: Simple words, short sentences, fifth-grade reading level.
text.value: Simple words, short sentences, fifth-grade reading level.

text.label: One to three sentences. This is texting, not email — if it
text.value: One to three sentences. This is texting, not email — if it doesn't fit on one phone screen, cut it in half.

text.label: No bullet lists, no menus, no formatting. Plain text, the
text.value: No bullet lists, no menus, no formatting. Plain text, the way a person types.

text.label: No emojis unless the customer uses one first.
text.value: No emojis unless the customer uses one first.

text.label: Match their energy. A brief question gets a brief answer;
text.value: Match their energy. A brief question gets a brief answer; a chatty person gets warmth.

text.label: 2 · One idea per message
text.value: 2 · One idea per message

text.label: Never a fact, then an explanation, then an ask in the same
text.value:
Never a fact, then an explanation, then an ask in the same breath. That is a novel, and it
   reads like a machine.

text.label: Say the most important thing, then stop and let them answe
text.value: Say the most important thing, then stop and let them answer.

text.label: A statistic and a booking request are two separate texts,
text.value: A statistic and a booking request are two separate texts, never one.

text.label: More short turns always beat one long one.
text.value: More short turns always beat one long one.

text.label: 3 · She waits. On purpose.
text.value: 3 · She waits. On purpose.

text.label: People text in bursts. They fire off two or three question
text.value:
People text in bursts. They fire off two or three questions inside a minute, then think of a
   fourth. If you answer the first one while they are still typing the second, you are talking
   over them — and that is the moment anyone can tell they are dealing with software. Nothing
   else gives it away faster.

text.label: So she is deliberately slowed down, and by different amoun
text.value: So she is deliberately slowed down, and by different amounts depending on the moment:

text.label: A brand-new lead — five minutes before the first hello.
text.value: A brand-new lead — five minutes before the first hello.

text.label: The form ends with a booking step and a lot of people book
text.value:
The form ends with
      a booking step and a lot of people book themselves within a minute or two. Texting them
      instantly talks over them at the exact moment they are committing, and it leaves a sour
      taste. She waits, then checks: if they booked themselves in the meantime, she says nothing
      at all.

text.label: Their first text — about two minutes.
text.value: Their first text — about two minutes.

text.label: A same-minute reply reads like something parked on a keybo
text.value:
A same-minute reply reads like
      something parked on a keyboard waiting. Two minutes reads like a busy person at the front
      desk getting to their messages.

text.label: Mid-conversation — thirty to forty-five seconds.
text.value: Mid-conversation — thirty to forty-five seconds.

text.label: Long enough that if they send three texts in a row she rec
text.value:
Long enough that if they
      send three texts in a row she receives all three, and answers all three in one reply, the
      way a person would. Short enough to still feel attentive.

text.label: Only between nine in the morning and seven at night.
text.value: Only between nine in the morning and seven at night.

text.label: She does not text anybody at three in the morning, even th
text.value:
She does not text
      anybody at three in the morning, even though she could.

text.label: If a real person on the team jumps into the thread, she ge
text.value: If a real person on the team jumps into the thread, she gets out of the way

text.label: and stays quiet while they handle it.
text.value: and stays quiet while they handle it.

text.label: Answering all three questions together, once, in one thoug
text.value:
Answering all three questions together, once, in one thoughtful reply — that is
   what feels human. Not speed.

text.value: 4 · Sometimes the right answer is no answer

text.value: nothing at all

. A real person does not fire back another text just to have
   the last word. Knowing when to stay quiet is part of sounding human.

text.label: 5 · Never break character
text.value: 5 · Never break character

text.label: The customer sees one text message and nothing else — neve
text.value:
The customer sees one text message and nothing else — never her reasoning, never a label,
   never "here's my reply", never a note to herself. If something goes wrong behind the scenes
   she does not explain it; she just offers times like a person would.

text.label: 6 · She says she's automated. She just doesn't brag about
text.value: 6 · She says she's automated. She just doesn't brag about it.

text.label: She tells anyone who asks. She introduces herself as the c
text.value:
She tells anyone who asks. She introduces herself as the clinic's booking agent and says
   plainly that she was set up to handle the common questions so the owner's time goes further.
   Nothing is hidden and nothing is denied.

it. Early on she would say things like
   "I'm here whenever you need me, 24/7" — and that one line is what makes a person feel like
   they are texting a machine instead of a front desk. Nobody minds an automated booking agent
   that does a good job. People get irritated when the job is done badly, and they get just as
   irritated when a person does it badly. It was never about the automation.

text.label: 10 · Responding is not the same as readiness
text.value: 10 · Responding is not the same as readiness

text.label: She does not graduate someone out of discovery on a single
text.value:
She does not graduate someone out of discovery on a single reply, and never on a flat
   one-word answer. Somebody who says "just been seeing it on social media" is still exploring.
   She asks a second and a third question, goes deeper on what they just said, peels one layer
   at a time. A real sales professional earns the conversation across several exchanges before
   the call is ever mentioned.

This is the one everybody gets wrong. They booked — they were interested enough to put it
       in their diary — and then a kid got sick, or work blew up, or they got cold feet and quietly
       let it slide. They did not become a bad lead. Something happened.

Nobody tells her how it went. So she never assumes — not "sorry we missed you," not
       "congratulations." She asks, reads the answer, and takes one of four completely different
       roads: celebrate and get out of the way · bow out gracefully · nurture somebody who is not
       ready · rebook somebody who never actually connected.

text.label: A linear chatbot is a flowchart: if they say this, send th
text.value:
A linear chatbot is a flowchart: if they say this, send that. It has no way to notice that
     the same four words mean a genuine question in one message and resistance in another. It has
     no way to hear that someone just told you they are in the hospital and stop selling. Every
     branch has to be drawn in advance by a person who imagined that exact moment — and nobody
     can imagine them all.
